items.title: A seminormal ring is reduced, and so is an absolutely weakly normal ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that seminormal rings and schemes are reduced and that absolutely weakly normal ones are as well (statement lines 12318-12322). The counted proof is a short direct argument: a nonzero element whose square is zero has its square equal to the cube of zero, so the defining property of seminormality would produce an element with zero square and a nilpotent cube, which is impossible (proof lines 12324-12328). It is H2: the argument is complete in the counted span and is deliberately short, and it is not dressed up as difficult.
